canonical_sources.title: Organization and Maintenance of Large Ordered Indices

pedagogy.problem_statement: In database storage engines, reading data from disk blocks is orders of magnitude slower than RAM access. Deep binary trees require dozens of random disk seeks per query, creating a massive I/O bottleneck.
pedagogy.core_thesis: B-Trees solve the disk bottleneck by packing hundreds of ordered keys into page-sized nodes, drastically increasing fan-out and reducing tree height so any record in billions requires only 3 to 4 disk page fetches.
pedagogy.mental_model: An indexed filing cabinet where each drawer holds hundreds of alphabetized index cards, allowing you to locate any document by checking only 3 drawers rather than opening 30 individual folders.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: B-Trees align search algorithms with hardware page boundaries, exchanging fast in-memory scans for minimal disk seeks.
verified_claims: A B-Tree node with fan-out B holds up to B-1 keys and B child pointers, matching the underlying filesystem block size (4KB to 16KB).
Tree height scales as O(log_B N); for 1 billion rows with B=500, tree height is at most 4, requiring only 4 disk seeks.
In contrast, a binary tree with B=2 has height log_2(10^9) ≈ 30, requiring up to 30 sequential disk round-trips.
B-Trees maintain perfect self-balancing: when a node overflows, it splits into two halves and pushes the median key upward.
anti_patterns: Do not imply the 'B' in B-Tree stands for Binary; B-Trees are high-fan-out multi-way search trees.
Do not represent disk access as byte-by-byte streaming; disks read and write in fixed-size hardware blocks or pages.
Do not show node splits growing downward; B-Trees grow upward from the leaves toward a new root.

scene_blueprint.title: The Disk I/O Bottleneck
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Establish the hardware latency gap: reading from disk is 100,000x slower than RAM, making random seeks catastrophic.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: RAM versus Disk latency comparison bars; high latency warning highlights the cost of disk seek cycles.

scene_blueprint.title: Binary Tree vs B-Tree Fan-out
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Contrast binary search trees (height 30, 30 seeks) with high fan-out B-Trees (height 3, 3 seeks) for one billion rows.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Tall 30-level binary tree with depth 30 appears on left; compact 3-level B-Tree with fan-out 500 appears on right.

scene_blueprint.title: Page Alignment & Traversal
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Illustrate how an entire disk page holding ordered keys is loaded in a single I/O and guides query routing.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Zoom into 8KB page container; golden query packet compares keys and traverses child pointer directly to leaf.

scene_blueprint.title: Balanced Growth: Node Split
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Demonstrate self-balancing growth: when a page fills up, the median key promotes upward, preserving logarithmic depth.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: An overflowing page splits in two; the median key ascends to parent level, maintaining uniform leaf depth.
